discussion_comments.comment_body:
Valid, fixed in b49479af3d.

The fallback now only picks an app that is still connected **and** still attached to the task: `sessionState.participants`, which `session.detach` and unregister already maintain. An app that detached is skipped, so the request goes to one that can still answer. If none is left, it fails right away instead of waiting.

The hub test now covers your scenario: owner, detached app and joined app, in that order. Against the previous code it picks the detached app; with the fix it picks the joined one. I also re-ran the end-to-end handoff: after the owner leaves, the joined app keeps the task running.

This one doesn't hold. Without `-m`, `git read-tree <tree1> <tree2>` reads both trees into stage 0; it only fails if they share a path, and a checkpoint's tracked tree and its untracked-files parent never do. Repro on git 2.43: read-tree of a tree with `a.ts` and a tree with `new.ts` gives `100644 ... 0 a.ts` and `100644 ... 0 new.ts`, and `write-tree` succeeds. The path is also covered by `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts`, whose checkpoints carry an untracked third parent (including an agent-created `new.ts`), and by a manual run where agent-created untracked files showed up in Last turn and Session.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Fixed. An entry whose value is an inline scalar, like `disabled: true` or `disabled: false # note`, is now a single line, so an indented comment after it stays with the author. Block scalars (`|`, `>`) and nested values still take their indented continuation lines with them. Test added for both disabling and re-enabling.

Fair point. Switched to splitting on `path.sep` only (same approach as the SDK's workspace file-indexer), so POSIX filenames containing a literal backslash are left intact. Added a POSIX-only test for that case.
